steps.text: Place cabbage in a stockpot; pour over enough water to cover. Add 1/4 teaspoon salt; bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Turn cabbage every 2 to 3 minutes; transfer any leaves that separate from cabbage into a strainer to drain and cool. Continue to boil until all the leaves have cooked, about 15 minutes. Reserve 1 1/2 cups of cabbage cooking water. Cut out the tough, thick center ribs of any large cabbage leaves with a sharp knife.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix ground beef, ground pork, cooked rice, eggs, onion, fresh parsley, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl until combined. Lay 1 cabbage leaf on a flat surface; place 1 heaping tablespoon of filling at the base of a cabbage leaf. Overlap with the bottom of the leaf; fold in side edges and roll up.
Repeat with remaining large cabbage leaves and filling.
Cut any leftover cabbage leaves into pieces and place in the bottom of a roasting pan. Layer stuffed cabbage rolls on top.
Combine tomato sauce, reserved cabbage water, white vinegar, and white sugar in a bowl; pour mixture over cabbage rolls. Cover roasting pan with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling is cooked through and sauce has thickened, about 2 1/2 hours. Baste stuffed cabbage rolls every hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Halupki (Stuffed Cabbage)
raw_recipe.description: This Ukrainian-style stuffed cabbage recipe features a hearty ground beef, pork, and rice filling topped with a tasty sweet-sour tomato sauce.

review.reviewBody: Hi, I'm Jillian the submitter of this recipe. I would like to correct a couple of things with this recipe: 1) Using a paring knife, remove the core of the cabbage then boil it (the leaves will come off easier that way) 2) In the list of ingredients after 1 (28 ounce) can tomato sauce it should read 12 oz. reserved cabbage water 3) Once you're done with step 9, then you take any leftover leaves, cut them up or (shred) and place into the bottom of a roasting pan and layer the stuffed cabbage rolls over top. I use large eggs and 90/10 lean ground beef when preparing these and sometimes sub fresh minced garlic for the garlic powder. (Also, 2/3 Tbsp. is 2 tsp. for the sugar) I've been making Halupki (stuffed cabbage) for years and my 98 year old Grandma has probably made thousands of these! She taught me how to make them and that's a memory I'll always treasure. We had such fun that day... Be sure to serve with mashed potatoes or sour cream and chive mashed potatoes for a twist. I hope you and your family enjoy these as much as everyone in my family does! UPDATE - It is with great sadness that I announce the passing of my Grandma Jean at the age of 104. June 26, 1914 - November 23, 2018. Love and miss you!!!!

I have always made mine in crockpot with tomatoes and sauerkraut (a must in this dish). I also core cabbage before immersing in water; and slice off the spine on each cabbage leaf after cooking. Cabbage stuffed with raw meat and cooked rice mixture. One of my all time favorites!! Always make extra, worth the time.

We really loved this dish! I did make some alterations for our taste (I used brown sugar instead of white, I used minute rice and added it to the meat mixture uncooked, I also added 2/3c finely diced carrot and 1-tBSP of Worcestershire sauce. I also used dry minced onion instead of fresh diced. My meat mixture was 2lb of pork & 1lb of ground turkey) and they turned out great. 100% will make again!

Two changes. The recipe was for 6 so adjust accordingly. Instead of tomato sauce I used a 15 oz can of dices tomatoes. All of the liquid and half of the tomatoes went into the sauce. The other half was added to the stuffing mixture. Also I added 1/4 cup of ricotta cheese for flavor. UMMM and AHHH were the comments.

***Pro tip***. Add 1 pack of Lipton onion soup mix to the rice meat and egg mixture no need for any other seasonings 2 Cans of Campbell’s tomato soup and instead of water use tomato juice. Top with 3 strips of uncooked bacon before cooking

Perfect; did not have tomato sauce, used two cans of tomato soup; apple cider vinegar because that’s what I had on hand. Added a large clove of garlic; minced, along with the onion, which I went a little heavy on. Also note: *used about half of one of the cans of tomato soup in the meat before mixing up. Used the rest of the soup with the recipe and altered the vinegar and sugar accordingly. Most definitely give it the full 2-1/2 hours! And definitely baste it! It begins thickening up nicely in those last 15-20 minutes. Gets good and thick, almost sticky on the bottom; still with lots of sauce. The house smells so nice on this rainy, cold winter day.

This is how I make mine (Hungarian descent). The only change I make is to take about 2 slices of bacon and boil it in water with a garlic clove and bay leaf. This makes a stock which I combine with the tomato sauce at the end. The bacon is then placed on top of the cabbage rolls. While mixing the filling, I usually add about 2 drops of liquid smoke.

I made it with what I had on hand: ground turkey. Seasoned with salt pepper onion garlic parsley paprika. I followed the instructions but I put it in my pressure cooker for 20. Minutes. . It was delicious. Melt in your mouth good. Will definitely make it again.

The basic recipe is what we always used. But... Everyone went crazy for Mom's "pigs in the blanket" (what we call this in W. Pennsylvania). The 2 secrets: We NEVER bake - we boil the cabbage rolls. For the sauce - add DICED ONION, and use KETCHUP. It makes a sweeter sauce! Mom learned to make this way 80 years ago as a small girl!

4.7.18 A tip from years ago from the Cabbage King cookbook made me prepare my cabbage leaves differently: freeze the entire head of cabbage, then defrost, cut out the core, and cabbage leaves just fall out. Sorry, I just couldn’t see all tomato sauce, so I used 1 can each of diced tomatoes and tomato sauce. I used what was on hand which ended up being more pork than ground beef, but all tasted fine. Made these cabbage rolls in the morning, refrigerated, and then into the oven for dinner for an easy, but tasty entree. These were very, very good cabbage rolls, served with mashed potatoes and freshly-cooked apples. Definitely would make again.

Hanging growing up eating polish and Czech and Hungarian food, halupki I love cabbage dishes. Due to terminal I learned how to make a few dishes and THIS is amazing. Generally as a result my hands don't function well so I didn't roll them.....I layer it like I would lasagne. Simplifies the process. If there are leftovers I take the halupki I made cabbage soup.

WOW!!! Authentic flavor if you’re looking to taste your childhood. My Mom and Gram were 100% Lithuanian and this tasted exactly like their recipe. My husband also said it was spot on his Mom’s recipe. Very simple to make. The most complicated step was prepping the cabbage and separating the leaves in the hot water. Otherwise it came together very easily and quickly. Don’t waste your time on the recipes using tomato soup.
Excellent!

I have been scaling recipes down to 1-2 dish meals. This one is great for using the meat in other dishes besides Halupki's. I rolled the meat mixture into large golf ball size portions and used some for the stuffed cabbage and then froze the other portions individually. I didn't like the taste of reheated cabbage... The best use I found is for smashed tacos - smash the ball sized meat onto a flour tortilla & fry (meat side down) until the meat is cooked through, turn over to cook the tortilla a bit, add shredded cabbage or lettuce and chipotle mayo sauce or salsa - yummy & easy!
We add more vinegar and sugar
Only substitution I made was ground turkey for the ground pork. This recipe is something my husband has been wanting for decades!
Halupkis are a favorite in our family. This is a great recipe but I add sauerkraut to the bottom of the pan instead of vinegar to the sauce and roast in the oven. Thanks for sharing.
My Mom Made Its all The Time, Especially Sundays And i Try Its its fell apart Will Try Its again, Very Soon
Great taste 👅
2 and a half hours is crazy! I sautéed the meat while fixing the rice.Then you stuff it and bake it just till bubbly like everything else!
